what: Regex answer parser (analysis/forced_answer.py:parse_number) checked against the estimate judge, before and after repair. See appendix A9.

method.note: Same seed both passes, so the two runs score the identical 200 answers.

causes.cause: U+202F narrow no-break space not normalised, so '80 000 000' parsed as three separate sub-1000 numbers and the scan fell through to a later figure
stripping every space made digits abut the following word; with no word boundary available the pattern backtracked onto a comma and truncated the number
'first number >= 1000' selects a survey year or a population figure rather than the estimate
causes.note: All four surviving disagreements. Fixing it changes the selection policy, which would move numbers across the report and needs its own labelled validation set.

root_cause_note: The two fixed bugs share an origin: the global space-stripping was itself the repair for the section 2.3 k=-1 bug (gpt-oss writing '45 300 000'). The corrected form removes spaces only between digit groups and anchors the word boundary on the scale word rather than the number.

impact_on_stored_answers.conclusion: Every gap shift is smaller than the confidence interval on the corresponding effect, so the report's conclusions stand.

not_repairable.reason: Resampling stored thresholded 0/1 outcomes, not completion text, so those runs cannot be re-parsed - only re-run.
not_repairable.why_A8_survives: The rate is 0% for Qwen3.5, so it cannot explain Qwen's degraded separation; and within a run it does not depend on position, while A8's load-bearing result contrasts early against late cuts in the same traces. A roughly uniform noise term lifts both halves together rather than creating a gradient, and inflates the floor, making those separations conservative.
